articles.title: Anthropic's debut rally fades as shares crack 7% in US pre-market trade

As traditional cost-saving strategies grow scarce, maintaining margins will be a challenge, compounded by the current economic environment affecting pricing strategies in the industry.

articles.title: Sebi plans consultation paper to remove FPI constraints absent in other markets
articles.content: SEBI is set to release a consultation paper aimed at simplifying regulations for foreign portfolio investors. The goal is to eliminate certain compliance restrictions to enhance India's appeal to global investors. SEBI also plans to expedite the onboarding process, targeting completion in just five business days. Additionally, KYC review cycles for applicable FPIs will be extended, reducing repetitive compliance activities.

articles.title: Indian finance hub eyes dual share model to kickstart public offers: Report
articles.content: Indian regulators are currently assessing a new proposal that would allow companies to introduce dual-class shares for listings in both domestic markets and GIFT City. This initiative seeks to invigorate equity market activity in GIFT City, which has faced challenges regarding limited primary market participation. One class of shares would be traded in rupees, while the other would be dollar-denominated, granting foreign investors easier access alongside reduced tax implications.

articles.title: Rupee rises past 93 vs USD as portfolio inflows, bear retreat fuel rally
articles.content: The Indian rupee has shown remarkable strength, breaking the 93 per dollar barrier for the first time since April. This positive shift was fueled by impressive foreign portfolio investments, exceeding $12 billion in November alone. Consequently, the rupee has left its Asian peers behind as it thrives against a strong dollar, all while navigating the Federal Reserve's anticipated hawkish stance, showcasing an encouraging signal for the Indian market.

articles.title: Rupee strengthens 17 paise to 93.15 against US dollar in early trade
articles.content: Rupee gained 17 paise to trade at 93.15 against the US dollar in early trade on Friday. The appreciation was supported by strong foreign fund inflows into the domestic equity markets. Despite higher crude prices and negative stock market sentiment, the currency showed resilience. Analysts expect slight positive bias in rupee trading due to declining crude and gold prices.

articles.content: Kristalina Georgieva, the head of the International Monetary Fund, has voiced her concerns regarding the overzealous excitement surrounding artificial intelligence.
